newsitem.title: NORWAY: Orkla, Tiger must sell some stock in UNI.
newsitem.headline: Orkla, Tiger must sell some stock in UNI.

text.p: Food-based conglomerate Orkla ASA and U.S. fund manager Tiger Management must reduce stock held in insurance group UNI Storebrand ASA to 10 percent before year-end, an Oslo Bourse statement said on Friday.

"UNI Storebrand has been informed that the finance department told Orkla ASA and Tiger Management, New York, yesterday that the finance department does not want to extend the dispensation for them to own up to 15 percent of shares in UNI Storebrand ASA," the statement said.

"Both shareholders have until December 31, 1996 to bring their ownership stakes in line with the law on finances under which no one may own more than 10 percent of share capital in a financial institution. The ruling can be appealed against within three weeks," the statement said.
It did not specify how big a stake in UNI the two shareholders have.
